findings:
🟡 [setsid-fallback-no-pgroup] CUT/FOLLOW-UP run.sh now spawns the child under `set +m`, so the last fallback (`exec bash`, neither setsid nor python3 present) no longer gives the child its own process group as G3 requires; the group kill and `ts_wait_pgid_gone` would then miss descendants. Excluded because flock and setsid both ship in util-linux, so a host that reaches snapshot mode almost always has setsid; smallest later fix is `set -m` around the spawn in that fallback only.
🟡 [setsid-branch-hard-ignored-signals] CUT/FOLLOW-UP the setsid branch relies on `trap - INT TERM QUIT PIPE XFSZ`, which bash cannot apply to signals already ignored when the outer shell started; the python3 branch, which resets them and calls `os.setsid()`, is now only second choice. Excluded because it is P4b behaviour outside the two repair findings and the inner run is no worse off than an in-place run under the same inherited dispositions; smallest later fix is to prefer the python3 branch when present.
🔵 [noflock-host-test-file] CUT/FOLLOW-UP on a host that really lacks flock, the P4b reaper cases in test-snapshot.test.sh call `flock ... sleep 30 &` unguarded and would go red in the in-place suite. Excluded because the spec scopes Finding 1 to the outer run.sh flow and the reaper, and the file already assumes rsync the same way.
🔵 [reaper-nits] CUT/FOLLOW-UP the `case` added to `_srr_pattern_match` duplicates entries already in `_SRR_PATTERNS`, and `ts_wait_pgid_gone` carries a dead `if [ "$n" -eq 0 ]; then :; fi` and defines `_ts_signal_session` globally from inside a function. Excluded as cosmetic with no behavioural impact.
